methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building in a non-metro region, creating potential for distributed deep capability if it activates peer networks beyond the campus—a key test of whether deep learning can escape concentration.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native targeting the 'technology gap' signals grassroots peer learning infrastructure in Hampton Roads, a distribution mechanism that could build deep capability outside traditional tech hubs if sustained beyond individual initiative.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student commentary explicitly naming data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide reveals awareness that current AI infrastructure concentrates economic benefit in NoVA while externalizing costs elsewhere—a pattern reinforcing neither depth nor distribution in underserved regions.

signals.title: Norfolk businesses are being urged not to miss out on the benefits of artificial intelligence - Rayo
signals.signal_reading: Businesses being 'urged not to miss out' on AI benefits suggests Hampton Roads enterprises are not yet adopting AI at scale, indicating shallow penetration even in Virginia's second-largest metro—a warning signal that distribution is failing even in population centers outside NoVA.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding an AI minor concentrates deep technical curriculum in an existing research university, potentially creating a knowledge hub in the New River Valley but requiring intentional distribution mechanisms to prevent becoming an isolated pocket that exports talent to NoVA.
